title: McGill 1993: csa fibre corrected of internal oblique at L3-L4 (M, supine)

imaging.modality: MRI Philips Gyroscan, spin echo TR 500 TE 20
imaging.plane: transverse slices (scanner axial, trunk in anatomic supine position); for each level the slice closest to the disc centre (within 5 mm)
imaging.level_definition: disc level: column labelled with the vertebra above the disc (e.g. "L3" = L3/L4), inferred from Table 5 which uses disc labels

quantity.name: csa_fibre_corrected
quantity.definition: anatomical CSA multiplied by cosine of fibre angle to the plane normal (authors may call it PCSA/physiological area; NOT volume/fibre-length PCSA); raw area x cosine of literature fibre line of action (Table 1: Dumas 1991, Macintosh & Bogduk, Santaguida); only muscles changing >10% listed; no SD

source.authors: McGill SM, Santaguida L, Stevens J
source.sample: 15 young men; healthy, no history of disabling back disease

how_to_simulate: Pose the model supine (lying; lordosis as when lying, no gravity load on trunk).

Select all internal oblique fascicles whose path crosses the plane at L3-L4 (transverse slices (scanner axial, trunk in anatomic supine position); for each level the slice closest to the disc centre (within 5 mm)), one side.
Sum their PCSA; use PCSA directly (fibre-angle corrected area).
Compare the one-side total with the measured mean +/- SD (bilateral sums are labelled side=bilateral_sum).

subject_model.source: Methods (SD age 3.6, weight 10.7, height 6.8); disc area Table 2

protocol.notes: Called "corrected cross-sectional area"; not volume/fibre-length PCSA.

extraction.check_notes: Table 5 read from rendered page 177 (disc labels printed).
